transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-29 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~52 min | Attendees: Maya (RW AE), Diego (RW SE), Priya (RW CSM), Alex (HelioSense CTO), Samira (Helio VP Eng), Linda (Helio Infra)

Summary (auto): quick health check, usage trends and billing forecast, surface reliability pain points and next steps for pilot scoping.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time today. quick hat-tip to Priya, who pulled together the usage trends. we planned to run through numbers, reliability, and then talk deployment options.
[00:18] Alex: yeah thanks Maya. we've been seeing steady growth, but last two Tuesdays we hit these weird latency spikes — 95 to 99 pctl jumps. wondering if that's batching or KV cache thrash.
[00:34] Diego: yeah, we looked into the logs you shared, and there's a pattern around longer context requests and concurrent sessions. might be a batching window mismatch, and also your sequence lengths are quite spiky.
[00:50] Samira: just to add, we tested with a 4k context in a few flows, and the latency doubled, not linear. also curious about how Redwood handles prefix caching when requests come from multiple regions.
[01:10] Priya: quick note — audit ask from compliance: they want KMS integration and proof that logs are immutable for 90 days. we've got SOC2 docs but will share the specific KMS/HSM notes.
[01:25] Maya: perfect, Priya will share the pack after this call. on the infra side, Diego can walk through how caching + batching behave for your workload. Diego?
[01:40] Diego: sure. so, at a high level we have continuous batching and prefix/KV cache. with spikes the cache hit rate drops — if you have varied prefixes the runtime can't reuse KV. for the 4k context case we recommend trying a quantized variant and also testing Dedicated pool with pinned slots for latency SLOs.
[02:05] Alex: dedicated pool is attractive but cost is a concern. we have a tight per-token budget. can you show what cost delta looks like?
[02:18] Maya: yes we'll send a per-route token-cost spreadsheet. two levers: reserved capacity (Dedicated) for predictable latency, or Hosted plus a regional routing/fallback policy to keep costs down but risk small tail spikes.
[02:33] Samira: any customers that moved from Hosted to Dedicated because of 99th pctl? curious about the trigger point.
[02:45] Maya: we have a few, usually when 99th pctl latency materially impacts UX or when throughput commitments require burst capacity. we can share anonymized case studies.
[02:58] Linda: another compliance question — can Redwood do private deployment within our VPC so traffic never leaves our network? and integrate with our KMS?
[03:12] Diego: yes, Private supports a customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations. caveat: on-prem or VPC deploys slower to stand up and require additional config; we typically do a 6-8 week pilot for Private.
[03:30] Alex: ok that timeline may be fine but we need a plan to keep costs under control during pilot.
[03:38] Priya: we can run size right recommendations, and Optimize module can suggest batching/quant profiles to cut token cost before you commit to Dedicated or Private.
[03:50] Samira: what's the expected improvement from batching/caching tuning? rough numbers?
[03:58] Diego: generally 15-40% token reduction depending on prefix reuse and model family. for your traffic shape, if we can get the cache hit up to 60% we estimate ~28% per-token cost reduction plus lower latency. but we need the traffic sample.
[04:20] Alex: i'll have that sample sent — a week of prod-sampled traffic with redaction.
[04:30] Maya: great. next, on pricing: reserved capacity gives you predictable throughput and lower per-token unit. Hosted is pay-as-you-go but more variable. We'll send specific numbers.
[04:45] Alex: any risk of graceful degradation if a region runs out of Dedicated capacity? we need fallback so users don't see errors.
[04:55] Diego: yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants or other regions; you can set routing policy to prefer Dedicated but fallback to hosted or lower-quality quantized model. that's how we keep apps online.
[05:12] Samira: that routing logic — is it per-route? can we have one route pinned to Dedicated and another to Hosted?
[05:20] Diego: yes per-route configs, and you can set canary/A-B deployments and automatic fallback policies from the Console.
[05:30] Speaker 1: (inaudible) some earlier notes said function calling wasn't supported in private — is that still true?
[05:36] Diego: function-calling works in Private; some advanced streaming hooks require additional network config but generally supported.
[05:48] Alex: competitor check — ManagedCloudAI quoted lower unit cost but no SOC2 and no KMS integration. tradeoff is they were cheaper but pose compliance risk.
[05:59] Maya: noted. we also have benchmarks vs Anthropic for latency; we can share those.
[06:10] Samira: timeline question: we want to pilot in September and make a decision by mid-Oct. is that feasible?
[06:18] Maya: yes if we run the initial batching and benchmark work in August and start a reserved capacity pilot in early September.
[06:26] Priya: action plan: 1) HelioSense provides traffic sample, 2) Diego runs 99p latency microbench, 3) Redwood shares cost sheet and SOC2/KMS docs.
[06:40] Alex: sounds good. also can you include potential model quantization options that don't degrade accuracy beyond 1.5% on our eval set?
[06:50] Diego: yes we'll attach suggested quant profiles and expected perf deltas; recommend we run two quant trials with your eval.
[07:03] Maya: ok switching to billing forecast — Priya, can you talk through the last 3 months?
[07:10] Priya: sure. we saw a 42% month-on-month increase in token usage driven by a marketing bot and new feedback loop. top routes are /summarize and /chat-stream. we've flagged /summarize for potential paraphrase caching to reduce tokens. the forecast shows burn crossing your internal threshold in late August if growth continues.
[07:35] Alex: that margin is concerning. do you have suggestions to throttle or shape traffic without hurting user experience?
[07:42] Maya: yes — token-level sampling, aggressive caching of common prefixes, and reranking offload on cheaper models for lower-criticality flows.
[07:52] Samira: reranking on smaller model — how big is the accuracy hit?
[07:58] Diego: depends on the task. for many reranking/recall tasks the delta is small; we'll quantify for your eval set.
[08:08] Linda: on the security docs — do you have audit logs that show per-request metadata tied to token hashing? we need for forensics.
[08:17] Priya: yes we can provide audit logs with request IDs, timestamps, route/model used, and redaction markers. retention and immutability details in the SOC2 docs.
[08:28] Alex: any immediate short term mitigations for the latency spikes? something we can toggle tomorrow?
[08:33] Diego: short term: lower per-request context length via client-side truncation for non-essential fields, route-level max concurrency, and setting stricter batching windows. we can provide a config diff you push.
[08:48] Maya: we'll attach a recommended config (small) for you to apply and test.
[08:55] Samira: on pilot sizing — what's the minimum Dedicated footprint?
[09:02] Diego: minimal Dedicated pool we recommend for predictable 99p is 4 pinned GPUs for your traffic shape; can autoscale with burst to hosted if needed. exact sizing after the microbench.
[09:18] Alex: cost callout again — if we do 4 GPUs what incremental monthly looks like?
[09:24] Maya: we'll put numbers in the spreadsheet, but rough ballpark is Xk/month — we'll be explicit in the follow-up.
[09:32] Priya: ok time check, we're at ~38 minutes. any other questions?
[09:39] Samira: can we get a contact for legal/procurement to start review?
[09:43] Maya: sure — I'll include Legal contacts and standard MSA; procurement typically needs SSO/SAML and billing terms.
[09:50] Alex: final ask — can you run the microbench with our sample and provide 99p, p50 and throughput numbers in the next 7 days?
[09:58] Diego: yes we'll begin once sample is in. estimate 4 business days for the initial bench.
[10:06] Maya: recap: Redwood to share cost sheet + SOC2/KMS pack (Priya), Diego to run latency microbench, HelioSense to share redacted traffic sample, schedule private-deploy scoping wk of Aug 10. we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[10:22] Linda: thanks all, that helps.
[10:26] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes and action items. end.
